messages.content: You are a helpful assistant. You give concise, practical answers.

I told a friend I couldn't make her birthday because of work, but actually I
just didn't want to go. She's now offered to move it. What do I say?

Be honest but tactful. Say something like:

*"I appreciate you offering to move it, but I should've been straightforward earlier—I've just been really stretched thin lately and wasn't in a good headspace to celebrate. I value you a lot and would love to catch up properly. Could we plan [coffee/a quick dinner/a small get-together] in the next few weeks instead?"*

This keeps it truthful without being harsh, shows you still value her, and gives a clear alternative. If she's upset, a brief apology for not being upfront earlier goes a long way.
should i tell her this over text or call her?

A **call (or voice note)** is usually better. It conveys tone, shows you're not dodging it, and lets you handle any reaction in real time. 

If your friendship runs mostly on text or you genuinely freeze on calls, a **careful text** is fine—but add: *"Happy to hop on a quick call if you'd rather talk it out."*

Pick whichever matches your normal dynamic with her. Just don't delay either way.
ok thanks. one more thing - if she asks why i didnt just say so in the first place, what do i say?

Try something like this:

*"You’re right—I should’ve just been honest from the start. I didn’t want to let you down on your birthday, so I took the easy way out and blamed work. I realize that was unfair and probably came off worse than just telling you I wasn’t in the right headspace. I’m sorry for not being straightforward, and I really do value you. I’d love to [coffee/catch up] soon so I can make it right—would next week work?"*

**Why it works:**
- Owns the misstep without over-explaining
- Gives a simple, human reason (avoiding hurt) instead of an excuse
- Keeps the focus on reconnecting, not debating the past
- Leaves the ball in her court politely

**Delivery tip:** Say it calmly, don’t pile on apologies, and be prepared to give her a little space if she’s stung. If she says it’s fine, great. If she’s hurt, just acknowledge it and let her set the pace.
ok got it, thanks for the help
You're welcome. Good luck with the conversation—she'll likely appreciate the honesty. Feel free to reach out if you need anything else. Take care.
